intervals.label: hosting RENO
intervals.note: CORRECTED 2026-09-18 (P0): RENO's own final-dataset paper (arXiv:2412.18711) confirms RENO data acquisition ended March 2023; this facility record's scope is specifically hosting RENO's detectors (the underlying nuclear power plant itself continues to operate independently of RENO).
intervals.quote: As of March 2023, the data acquisition was completed after a total of 3800 live days of detector operation.

intervals.label: completed (hosting RENO)

intervals.quote: As of March 2023, the data acquisition was completed after a total of 3800 live days of detector operation.

name: Yonggwang (Hanbit) Reactor Neutrino Site
notes: RENO's own official site domains (reno.snu.ac.kr, home.kias.re.kr/MKG/h/reno) failed DNS/connection when tried; this record relies on the 2012 arXiv discovery paper, INSPIRE, and the Hanbit Nuclear Power Plant's Wikipedia page (used only for an approximate regional coordinate).

operator.note: No source consulted (checked 2026-09-17) states an operator of the RENO experimental site distinct from the RENO collaboration and the adjacent Hanbit Nuclear Power Plant (operated by KHNP, whose own page was not consulted).

summary.plain: The site near the Hanbit (formerly Yonggwang) nuclear power plant in South Korea where the RENO experiment placed two detectors to catch antineutrinos from six reactors.
summary.technical: Reactor-neutrino site at the Hanbit (Yonggwang) Nuclear Power Plant, South Korea, hosting the RENO near (294 m) and far (1383 m) detector halls, 6 × 2.8 GW_th reactor array.
